html:
The imperial dynasty that ruled China from 1368 to 1644, between the Mongol Yuan and the Manchu Qing. It was the last dynasty of China led by Han Chinese.

Its founder, Zhu Yuanzhang, the Hongwu Emperor, rose from poor peasant to rebel leader and drove out the Mongols. He wanted a fixed society of self-sufficient villages and a huge hereditary army, and he ruled harshly, purging tens of thousands of officials. His son, the Yongle Emperor, seized the throne in 1402 and moved the capital to Beijing, where he built the Forbidden City.

What the Ming is known for:

  • Zheng He's voyages, seven great fleets that sailed to Southeast Asia, India, Arabia and East Africa between 1405 and 1433, then stopped.
  • The Great Wall mostly as it stands today, rebuilt in brick and stone against the Mongols.
  • Blue and white porcelain from Jingdezhen, and novels such as Journey to the West.

From the 16th century China was drawn into world trade. Silver from Japan and from Spanish America, via the Manila galleons, flowed in to pay for silk and porcelain, and the state began to collect taxes in silver. New crops such as maize and sweet potatoes arrived. Jesuits like Matteo Ricci reached the court.

The end came in the 1630s and 1640s, with cold years, famines, falling silver imports and a bankrupt state. Rebels under Li Zicheng took Beijing in 1644 and the last emperor hanged himself. A Ming general then let the Manchus through the wall, and they founded the Qing.
sum: The imperial dynasty that ruled China from 1368 to 1644, between the Mongol Yuan and the Manchu Qing. It was the last dynasty of China led by Han Chinese.
